floor_history.headline: Recon: floor 25 -> 14 in pure C (cheat scaffold dropped, worth 0); residual is now register-name-only, 136 vs 136 insns, in exactly two clusters.
Floor 14 -> 8: moving `i = 0;` inside the loop guard closed the whole callee-save cluster; both session-1 frontier mechanisms measured dead and replaced with instrumented successors.

Floor holds at 8 (17 more structural forms, none below); session 2's K4 is CORRECTED — the $s0/$s1 flip IS global.c:allocno_compare, and both residual clusters are now stated as exact allocator arithm

frontier.hypothesis: F4' — the 2-point delay-slot residue is now a closed-form inequality: with `i = 0;` pre-`rand()` the counter allocno sits at priority 6153 against `h`'s 8750, so the flip needs either counter n_refs >= 6 or `h` live_length > 22.7. The remaining untried surface is lowering `h`'s n_refs from 7 to 4 (floor_log2(4)*4/16 = 5000 < 6153) WITHOUT splitting the variable.
frontier.mechanism: global.c:allocno_compare, priority = floor_log2(n_refs)*n_refs/live_length*10000, ties broken by allocno number; whichever of {counter, h} is allocated first takes $s0(16). Session 3 measured every parameter of both allocnos directly.
frontier.next_probe: Respell the case-20 arithmetic so `h` is referenced fewer times without splitting it into separate locals (which K2/K3 already killed): fold `h = D_800A37A8[a0_val]; if (...) h |= 0x8000; func_80060414(h, ...)` into forms with one or two `h` references (e.g. compute the ORed value in a temporary and pass it, or select between two expressions), then read `h`'s n_refs/live_length/priority straight out of `bash tmp/grind/func_800174F4/s3/alloc.sh <tag>` BEFORE scoring. Any form whose `h` priority drops under 6153 is then re-measured with the pre-`rand()` `i = 0;` in place.

frontier.hypothesis: F5' — cluster (A) (6 of the 8 points) needs BOTH reg 3 and reg 4 in the selector allocno's `hard_reg_conflicts U regs_someone_prefers`; it currently has conflicts {2,29} and all three preference sets empty. The working precedent inside the same function is pseudo 99, which skips reg 4 only because lower-priority conflicting allocno 101 prefers 4.
frontier.mechanism: global.c:find_reg allocates the lowest-numbered register of the class outside that union; prune_preferences populates regs_someone_prefers from the hard_reg_full_preferences of lower-priority CONFLICTING allocnos. config/mips/mips.h defines no REG_ALLOC_ORDER.
frontier.next_probe: Search for a C shape in which the dispatch value's allocno conflicts with an argument-position-preferring allocno while still dying before `func_8005D46C` (crossing that call forces callee-save — the measured 29/138 form). Verify every candidate with `bash tmp/grind/func_800174F4/s3/findreg.sh <tag> 120` FIRST: the dump shows directly whether conflicts/someone_prefers moved, which the score does not. If no shape moves those sets, cluster (A) is a genuine allocator lock and the function is a candidate for the endgame-lock disposition after the remaining modalities.

frontier.hypothesis: F6 — a directed permuter campaign from the floor-8 base closes the register-name residual. Still unrun (proposed in s1 as F3, re-proposed in s2); the base is now 6 points closer than when it was first proposed and is a clean 136-vs-136 register-name-only diff, the shape decomp-permuter's weighted register scoring searches well.
frontier.mechanism: decomp-permuter randomizes statement order, temporaries and types and scores against a single-function target.o; the two residual clusters are pure register-name substitutions with zero insert/delete/reorder, so the search space it explores is exactly the one that matters here.
frontier.next_probe: Build the single-function target.o from asm/funcs/func_800174F4.s + tools/decomp-permuter/prelude.inc (drop `.set gp=64`) per .claude/rules/difficult-is-not-impossible.md so the base score is the real weighted diff; seed from memory/grind/func_800174F4/candidate.c; run a fresh-seed campaign with tools/permuter_campaign.py, doing launch, `wait --dir <ws>` and `harvest --stop` all inside a single turn (see [[grinder-permuter-orphan-stop-gate]]).
